probes.reading: Apply SAP page-11 plain visit-date minus randomization-date subtraction to published upstream REF.ADT and REF.TRTSDT, then use the same native <=1 baseline and CIBIC+ windows and Define code-label mapping. SAP page-9 randomization at Visit 3 and Define ADSL.TRTSDT/ADQSCIBC.TRTSDT (citations 7-9) identify the date anchor; citation 11 identifies the assessment-date source. This changes the arithmetic from the literal REF.ADY reading, without inserting the post-reference +1. On LOCF rows this computes the retained date's donor window; it does not reconstruct or assume a recipient-date rule.

Window observed records by ADY as the literal reading does, but give each LOCF record the expected visit it was created for instead of the window of its carried ADY, as R Consortium Pilot 6's later R program adqscibc.r (a reference reimplementation, not the submission's own program) does: lines 155-160 list the expected visits Week 8, 16 and 24, lines 162-166 create LOCF records for them with derive_locf_records, and lines 172-175 keep the carried record's ADY and ADT. The Define window rule does not say how LOCF records get their visit. The LOCF branch reads the visit the reference record is keyed under (an expected visit 8, 16 or 24), so this reading checks only that observed records follow the ADY windows and that LOCF records are not re-windowed by their carried day.

interpretations: Native SAP.pdf physical page 11 (printed page 10), section 8.2 table, shows an underlined less-than sign (<=1) for Baseline. The exact-section text loses the underline and reads < 1. This is a text-representation artifact, not a contradiction between documents. The literal probe follows the native <=1 boundary.

SAP section 8.2 uses visit date minus randomization date. The new SAP page-9 statement places randomization at Visit 3, Define ADSL.TRTSDT sources the Visit 3 SV start date, and Define ADQSCIBC.TRTSDT copies ADSL.TRTSDT (citations 7-9). These statements identify a citable Visit 3 date anchor, correcting the prior statement that no raw randomization-date source was identified. They do not equate plain subtraction with the post-reference +1 in ADQSCIBC.ADY (citation 10).

The literal Define-directed windowing probe uses published upstream ADY on every reference row. It does not silently substitute AWTARGET for LOCF records; the documents do not state that AVISITN override.

The added SAP_DATE_WINDOW reading reads only the published upstream REF.ADT and REF.TRTSDT. It does not read the current target AVISITN as a calculation input, derive dates from the maintained yamaa ADSL output, or choose raw SV records. Missing upstream dates propagate to a missing window; no date completion, duplicate-visit tie-break, population eligibility filter, or dose-date substitution is added.

Both the existing Define-directed literal and the added SAP date-window reading evaluate a window using each reference row's retained upstream day or date. In the maintained LOCF rows, ADY and ADT are copied from DONOR16 or DONOR24 while AVISITN is assigned to a recipient visit. The new Visit 3 anchor evidence does not specify a recipient assessment date or authorize substituting AWTARGET for retained donor day/date.

The SAP summary-visits statement in citation 6 supports Week 8, Week 16 and Week 24 as analysis visits. It does not fully specify the AVISITN assignment for every LOCF recipient, the creation/eligibility of recipient rows, or donor selection. The new date-window output therefore leaves donor-window versus recipient-visit applicability open for review.
The published matching fields STUDYID, USUBJID, PARAMCD, AVISITN and QSSEQ remain direct REF copies. AVISITN__SAP_DATE_WINDOW is a separate computed output, and its helper is _CIBC_FU_SAP_DAY.

The program citations 12-16 come from R Consortium Pilot 6's later R program adqscibc.r (a reference reimplementation, not the submission's own program). They show how the reference values can be produced, not what the original authors intended, and they do not document the LOCF recipient-visit rule; they support the AVISITN__LOCF_RECIPIENT_VISIT reading only.
claims.assessment: The new statements supply the missing documentary Visit 3 date-anchor chain and allow a separate SAP date-subtraction reading. They leave the SAP subtraction versus Define ADY arithmetic choice and the application of donor-day windows to LOCF recipient visits unresolved. Program tracing: R Consortium Pilot 6's later R program adqscibc.r (a reference reimplementation, not the submission's own program) windows observed records by ADY (lines 104-112) but creates each LOCF record for an expected visit from its cibic_expected_obsv table (lines 155-160, 162-166), keeping the carried record's ADY and ADT (lines 172-175); it does not re-window LOCF records by their carried ADY. The added AVISITN__LOCF_RECIPIENT_VISIT reading states that; its LOCF branch can only take the visit the record is keyed under, so it tests the observed-record windows and that LOCF records are not re-windowed.
claims.question: For observed CIBIC+ assessments, should AVISITN follow SAP plain date subtraction or Define-directed ADY with its post-reference +1? What documented AVISITN recipient-visit rule should apply to LOCF rows whose retained ADY and ADT describe the donor?

claims.rule: Read QS.QSSTRESN for CIBIC observations; missing postbaseline CIBIC+ values use the last targeted analysis observation carried forward, and CIBIC+ does not use item-score prorating.

citations.quote: QS.QSSTRESN, where QS.QSTESTCD = CIBIC

The last observation carried forward
(LOCF) algorithm only considered records used for analysis as candidates to carry forward.

Records where
ANL01FL=’Y’ are the ones that were used for analysis.

Records where DTYPE=’LOCF’ signify those where AVAL was imputed using the LOCF
algorithm.

Source data can be traced back to the SDTM.QS domain using USUBJID and
QSSEQ.

Missing postbaseline efficacy values will be imputed using last observation carried
forward (LOCF).  Missing baseline values and missing safety data will not be imputed.
For the efficacy data, the last observation carried forward will be based on the targeted
assessments (i.e. those assigned to be the analyzable assessment based on the assessment
windows).

If multiple assessments fall into the same visit window (windows
defined in following table), then the assessment closest to the target day will be selected.
[Note that retrieval visits (visit number 201) are included for the purpose of selecting
assessments for the week 24 visit window.] If two assessments are equidistant from the
target day, then the assessment prior to the target day will be selected.  In situations
where imputation of missing values is also involved, imputation will use the targeted
